Johnny C. Garcia

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 35, Bexar County, Texas · Open seat

Bexar County Sheriff's Office deputy and public information officer

Johnny C. Garcia, 38, was born and raised on San Antonio's west side and has worked in law enforcement with the Bexar County Sheriff's Office for nearly two decades. He advanced from the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary and defeated Maureen Galindo in the May 26, 2026 runoff to win the Democratic nomination for the redrawn 35th Congressional District. He faces Republican Carlos De La Cruz in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Garcia stands

Tariffs and economy
Supports ending the Trump tariffs, saying they raise prices and put at risk the Texas jobs that depend on trade. Supports relief for working and middle-class taxpayers and investment in American manufacturing.
Jobs and workforce
Proposes expanding apprenticeships, job training, and public-private partnerships to connect workers with high-wage jobs. Supports small businesses.
Health care
Supports renewing ACA subsidies, strengthening the Affordable Care Act, expanding Medicaid, lowering prescription drug costs, and increasing mental health services.
Immigration
Supports bipartisan comprehensive immigration reform that includes border security, orderly pathways to citizenship, work visas, and funding for immigration courts to reduce backlogs.
Public safety
Supports giving officers training, resources, and mental health support, along with transparency and oversight. Supports youth programs, mental health services, and community partnerships to prevent crime.
Education
Supports fully funded public schools, investment in teachers, and affordable pathways to college, apprenticeships, and vocational training.
Congressional authority
Says Congress should reassert its authority over tariffs and the budget. Supports reversing cuts to the Department of Education, FEMA, the FAA, and other agencies.

Background

  • Deputy, Bexar County Sheriff's Office, for nearly two decades: jail, patrol, SWAT team, hostage negotiator
  • Public information officer, Bexar County Sheriff's Office
  • Earlier worked in construction
  • Graduate of Memorial High School (Edgewood ISD), San Antonio
  • Attended St. Philip's College
  • Won the 2026 Democratic runoff for TX-35 over Maureen Galindo; first run for office (described as a political newcomer)
